seoTitle: How to Add a Tracking Number to an eBay Order
metaDescription: Learn how to add or edit a tracking number on a sold eBay item from desktop or mobile, and why timely tracking protects your seller account.
intro: Adding a tracking number after you ship an item confirms the sale for the buyer and protects you if a delivery dispute ever comes up. It's a two-minute task once you know where eBay hides it, but the option sits a few clicks deep inside the sold order itself, not on the main Selling dashboard. This guide walks through finding the order, attaching the carrier and tracking number, and what happens automatically once you save it, whether you're shipped a single item or working through a batch of sold orders.

steps.heading: Open My eBay and go to Selling
steps.body: From any eBay page, click the My eBay dropdown near the top right of the screen. It opens a full list of account sections — Summary, Bids/Offers, Watchlist, Purchase History, and further down, Selling. Choosing Selling takes you to your My eBay Selling Overview, which shows quick counts for Active listings, Orders, and Unsold items along with a 90-day sales total. This overview is your starting point any time you need to manage an order rather than browse the marketplace.

image.caption: The My eBay account dropdown open above the Selling Overview page, where Active, Orders, and Unsold counts give a quick snapshot of your account.

steps.heading: Find the sold, shipped item in your orders
steps.body: From Selling, switch to the Orders tab or the Sold section, which lets you filter by status — Awaiting shipment, Shipped, Awaiting feedback, and so on. Locate the item you've already packed and dropped off or scheduled a pickup for. If you're managing several sales at once, sorting by 'Time ended: recent first' keeps the newest orders at the top so you're not hunting through weeks of history for the one you just shipped.

steps.heading: Open the order's action menu
steps.body: Each sold order has an Actions column with a 'More actions' dropdown. Opening it reveals the full set of things you can do to that specific order: Add tracking number, Mark as shipped, Leave feedback, View order details, View PayPal transaction, Contact buyer, and Cancel order. The order line itself also shows a direct 'Tracking number: [Add]' link next to the buyer's details, which is often the faster route if you can see it on screen already.

image.caption: The order's More actions menu, with Add tracking number sitting above Mark as shipped and Leave feedback.

steps.heading: Select the carrier and enter the tracking number
steps.body: Clicking Add tracking number opens a small form asking for the shipping carrier — USPS, FedEx, UPS, DHL, or another courier from the dropdown — and a field for the tracking number itself. Type or paste the number exactly as the carrier gave it to you; eBay checks it against the carrier's own tracking data, so a mistyped digit means the buyer sees no movement even though the package is actually in transit. Save the entry once both fields are filled in correctly.

steps.heading: Let eBay notify the buyer automatically
steps.body: Once you save valid tracking details, eBay updates the order status to shipped and emails the buyer the carrier and tracking number without any extra step from you. This is the main reason to add tracking promptly rather than batching it for later — buyers who can see their package moving are far less likely to open a case or leave a worried message asking where their order is.

steps.heading: Edit tracking if the details change
steps.body: If you picked the wrong carrier, mistyped the number, or reshipped the item, go back into the same order and the action menu will now show an edit option in place of Add. Update it the same way; eBay refreshes the buyer-facing tracking link automatically once you save the correction.

steps.heading: Handle late tracking numbers and mobile updates
steps.body: If a courier hasn't issued a number yet at drop-off, mark the item as shipped so the buyer isn't left with an unshipped order on their end, then come back and add the tracking number the moment the carrier provides it. The eBay mobile app mirrors this whole flow — open Selling, find the order, and Add tracking number is available from the same order details screen. Leaving orders untracked for too long can affect your seller performance metrics, so treat tracking as part of the shipping process itself, not an optional follow-up.

faq.question: What happens if I forget to add tracking on eBay?
faq.answer: Without tracking, you have less protection if a buyer claims non-receipt, and consistently missing tracking can negatively affect your seller performance standing over time.

faq.question: Can I add tracking from the eBay mobile app?
faq.answer: Yes, the mobile app lets you add or edit tracking numbers on sold orders through the same Selling and order-details flow as the desktop site.

faq.question: Does adding tracking automatically mark the item as shipped?
faq.answer: Yes, entering a valid tracking number updates the order status to shipped and triggers eBay's automatic email notification to the buyer.

faq.question: What if my carrier doesn't provide a tracking number?
faq.answer: For carriers without trackable service, you can still mark the item as shipped without a number, though this offers less protection than a trackable shipment if a dispute comes up.

faq.question: Where exactly is the Add tracking number option?
faq.answer: Go to My eBay > Selling > Orders, find the sold item, and open its 'More actions' dropdown. Add tracking number is listed there, and often as a direct link on the order row itself.
